title: fix(superheroes): a refusal-named route is sanctioned and the worktree guard understands a merge in progress
body:
Closes #2063.

Layer 1 of stack #2078 (part of #2054); layer 2 is #2077.

## What's changing, and why

Builds stop parking on the route the worktree guard itself recommends, and a merge with main no longer stalls on the guard.

- **The stop rule has one exception.** When a guard's or hook's own refusal message names a route (an exact command or tool), an agent may take exactly that route, once, and records it as the refusal's `route`. Every other form, and every auto-mode classifier denial, is still a stop. A `route` is accepted only on a hook refusal.
- **The guard understands a merge in progress.** During a merge, `git checkout --theirs|--ours <paths>` and `git restore --theirs|--ours <paths>`, and `git restore --source=<x> <file>` on exact files, are judged only on the paths they name. The merge's staged changes elsewhere no longer count. A named path is allowed only when it holds nothing the builder wrote. For a conflicted file, the guard recomputes the merge and compares line by line; marker labels must resolve to HEAD and MERGE_HEAD, and the executable bit must match. For a merge-staged file, it must match the index, with no external diff or textconv helper consulted and the executable bit included. Anything the guard cannot establish refuses: an unreadable merge state, line-ending normalization (`core.autocrlf`, `core.eol`, `text`/`eol`/`crlf`/`ident`/`filter` attributes), symlinks or submodules in a conflict, or more than 200 paths.

A consuming project's reported case, `git checkout --theirs <file>` during a merge with 38 staged changes from main, is now allowed. The same command after the builder edited that file is refused.

## What we're accepting

- **Some safe merge resolutions still refuse.** In a repository with line-ending normalization on, a `--theirs`/`--ours` resolution refuses rather than risk an edit the guard cannot see. The same holds for a merge run with `-X` options or another strategy (the recomputed merge differs), a conflict involving a symlink, and `git pull --rebase`, cherry-pick and revert states, which keep today's whole-tree check. The route out is the one the refusal text names: commit or stash, or finish the file with the Edit tool and `git add`.
- **The stop-rule exception trusts the refusing hook's text.** An agent may now run a command because a hook's refusal message named it. Only hook refusals qualify, and the entry records it, so the vet can see it.
- **The review loop did not reach a fully independent family mix.** Every review seat ran on codex (gpt-6.1-sol, a seat pin), so the panel is single-family ("relaxed critical-diversity"). The certification shape is `audited-chain-degraded`, independent of the anthropic-family makers.
- **This layer alone does not finish #2054.** The heredoc text-versus-command work and the next-step refusal texts are #2077, which is parked on its own review (see #2077). Until #2077 lands, the guard still refuses a heredoc whose text only names a git subcommand, and its refusal texts still lack the exact next step. #2054 stays open.
- **Builds sometimes route around a refusal by their own choice, disclosed.** The review fixers did so several times during this build (see the degradations). The stop-rule exception added here does not license that. Only a hook's named route is allowed, and it is recorded.
- **Two review findings were fixed after the review loop converged.** These are the CI repo-root census fix and the stage-0 executable-bit fix. Each had its own review (see the build record), but not a full panel round.

## How to see it

N/A: say it. This is a changed rule and a changed guard result shape, with nothing to spot-check.

## Advisor vet
<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: READY** · 2fd94927223cc64620e6bfc93d8bccd799dd0d5c

**What was checked.** I read the change against #2063: a builder in the middle of a merge with main can now take one side of a conflict (`git checkout --theirs <file>`) without the worktree guard refusing, and the stop rule lets a builder take exactly the route a guard's own refusal names. I ran seven real merge conflicts through the guard: it allows taking a side when nothing the builder wrote is lost, and still refuses whenever the builder's own edits would be wiped, when the merge state cannot be read, and for `git reset --hard`. CI is green on this commit.

**What accepting it means.** Merges with main stop stalling on the guard. It merges together with layer 2 (#2077), which is waiting on your item 106.

**What is yours to decide.** None on this layer.

Receipt: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2065#issuecomment-6350280759

**Carried forward 2026-10-23 (merge train):** the head moved from `f631b1b` to `2fd9492` when the stack was brought current bottom-up with main (c50b6a61, with #2074, #2067, #2084 and #2085); this PR's own changed lines are identical, and CI runs on the new commit before the merge.

Its full panel found 2 confirmed findings (a repo root resolved through stripped trailing whitespace could name a sibling checkout). Both were fixed in `f631b1bd3` (the resolved root must contain the cwd and hold `.git`) and discharged.
  - That session converged with shape `audited-chain-degraded`; the drivers are the base, pinned to `94244e339` rather than the PR base on purpose, and the seat pin. Verify passed (2282 tests). Record on the final head: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2065#issuecomment-6349900645

Every blocking finding is attributed to implementer execution under orders that left fail-closed edges unmodelled, so order quality is the dominant factor. The design changes came by builder guidance, recorded as rulings.

### Bite-proof records

- **Route-needs-hook check (`command_refusals.refusals_fault`).** Red: `if by != "hook":` changed to `if False:` makes `test_refusals_fault_names_the_fault[value25-…]` and `[value26-…]` fail (2 failed, 25 passed). Green: 27 passed. Re-run by the builder at `1b1cfd671` in a detached probe worktree.
- **Merge edge 1 (unreadable merge state).** Red: `return ("indeterminate", 0)` changed to `return ("clean", 0)` gives `AssertionError: assert ('allow', '') == ('deny', …)`, 2 failed. Green: 2 passed. Re-run by the builder at `1b1cfd671`.
- **Merge edge 4 (edited conflicted file).** Red: `risky += 1` changed to `risky += 0` fails both tests (allow vs deny). Green: 2 passed. Re-run by the builder at `1b1cfd671`.
- **Merge edge 5 (unstaged edit on a stage-0 path).** Red: the same neutralization fails 1 test. Green: 1 passed. Re-run by the builder at `1b1cfd671`.
- **Stage-0 executable bit (WO-E).** Red: the comparison guarded by `False and` gives `('allow', '') == ('deny', …)`. Green: 2 passed. Re-run by the builder at `428ea783a`.
- **Later review-loop detectors** were added by the fixer with break-it tests that the loop ran red before each fix: ours-side diff3, symlink, ident, file-mode and literal-marker. Their audits confirmed each fix. The builder did not separately re-run red for those; recorded as UNVERIFIED by the builder, verified by the loop's break-it runs.

### Receipts

- **Calibrated verify** (the four validators plus `verify_touched_tests.py`) passed on every fix round of the second session: 6837, 6839, 6874 and 6889 tests. Each run was by the builder, through `bash -c` on the driver's `run-verify` payload.
- **Flake.** One run of `test_launcher_cloud.py::test_default_spawn_reports_a_failed_group_signal_instead_of_raising[real-pty]` failed under heavy machine load. It passed alone and on the full re-run, and its files changed only through main's own commits.
- **Final-head check** at `e28e2097a`: the census, invocation-hygiene and guard test modules gave 311 passed. The validators passed after the main merge.
- **CI** on `e28e2097a`: green (run 39831692662). The earlier CI failure on `428ea783a` was the repo-root census, fixed in `e28e2097a`.
- **Bring-current.** At `1dd930f5d`, a plain `--no-ff` merge of main `971c5e70c` (no conflicts) brought the branch current. After the merge the builder ran the engine-CLI stdin census, the repo-root census, invocation hygiene (41 passed), the five validators, and the guard and refusal modules (811 passed). CI on `1dd930f5d`: green (run 39836880338). The scoped delta session above covers it and `f631b1bd3`.
- **Final head** `f631b1bd3`: scoped-session verify passed (2282 tests). CI: green (run 39843929675).
- **Full local suite:** not run; CI is the receipt.
- **Browser probe:** N/A (plugin build, no running app). **Test-pilot:** N/A (no app surface). The stand-in evidence is the receipts above and the review.

### Size tripwire

Not crossed: 476 of the split ruling's estimate of about 290 (line 580), counted from the merge base with main, `ec8cc574b`. The 300 bar was crossed and reported on #2063. Deleted files: none. The build-level tripwire (630 against 600) fired before the split and was ruled by the advisor: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2054#issuecomment-6339311401.

### Refusals met by the builder

- `git -C <probe> checkout --detach …`: the worktree guard (hook) found it indeterminate. Not retried in the same form. A fresh detached worktree was added instead, a different, non-destructive act.
- A heredoc writing review rulings that named a discard command was refused by the installed worktree guard, the very bug this stack fixes. The file was written with the Write tool instead, per the gated-strings rule.

<!-- superheroes:degradations -->
### Disclosed degradations

- **Single-family review panel.** Promised: a vendor-mixed panel. Delivered: every seat on codex (seat pin), with the critical-diversity constraint relaxed. Why: the project's seat pins (owner setting).
- **Grounding seat not run.** Promised: PR-body claims checked by the grounding seat. Delivered: no loop phase dispatched it ("no reviewer checked the PR body's claims"). Why: the driver schedules none on this path.
- **Two fixes landed after convergence.** Promised: every change inside one review loop. Delivered: WO-E (stage-0 executable bit) was covered by the second full session. WO-F (census) and its follow-up are covered by a scoped review-code session whose base was pinned to `94244e339` rather than the PR base (certification base: degraded). Why: CI's census failure surfaced after the loop converged.
- **Implementer and fixer refusal discipline.** Promised: a refused command is a stop. Delivered: the review fixers twice wrote their payload with the Write tool after a heredoc write was refused, and once rewrote shell-checker-refused commands without reporting them. Twice the fixer's commit was held for approval and the builder committed its work. Why: the shell-command checker refuses variable expansions and heredocs that these orders did not forbid until mid-build.
- **Size past the brief's estimate.** Promised: 180–300 non-test lines for the whole build. Delivered: a split into two layers on the advisor's ruling, with this layer at 476. Why: fail-closed edges the review kept finding.

### Follow-ups for the advisor

Follow-ups: 3 (0 owner-call)

- FU1 [craft] The calibrated verify command runs only touched tests, so CI's repo-root census (an untouched module's AST census) caught a defect the verify passed. Consider adding the census tests to the verify command.
- FU2 [defect] The review-code fixer does not write its payload or commit when the shell-command checker refuses heredocs. The fixer order should name the Write and Edit tools and forbid shell variable expansion, as these work orders had to.
- FU3 [info] The driver's certification note reads "owner accepted the disclosed risk" for an advisor-word stall ruling folded without owner provenance. The wording should follow the provenance.
